title: Shield workshop - remediation playbook & KMS handoff
summary: Review of recent penetration test observations and agreement on a prioritized remediation playbook, patch cadence, and KMS handoff details. Discussed RBAC/SSO gaps, audit logging retention needs, data residency constraints for EU customers, and a short-term mitigation plan plus pilot timeline for KMS integration.

Customer to share asset inventory export and segmentation map by 2026-07-05
Schedule 30-minute KMS onboarding pilot on a staging tenant (tentative 2026-07-13)
Follow-up call to review progress and baseline patch cadence (1 week after doc share)

transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-07-01
- Time: 15:00 UTC
- Duration: 72 minutes
- Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE); Priya Nair (Redwood SE); Marta Reyes (BlueHarbor CISO); Daniel Wu (Head of Platform); Leah Kim (Sr. Sec Eng)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be partial):
- Main: Pen test results review; agreed to triage by risk and impact, short-term mitigations, and KMS pilot for key encryption needs.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I think we have a full agenda, we'll run through the red team findings, then remediation playbook and the KMS handoff. Marta thanks for coordinating.
[00:12] Marta Reyes: Yeah thanks Alex. Quick note, we distributed the red team report this morning, there's a lot in there — some noise but also a couple high risk items we want to make sure get triaged fast.
[00:20] Priya Nair: Cool, should we start with the high sev issues? I flagged the auth bypass and the misconfigured storage ACLs as top of list.
[00:30] Leah Kim: Yeah the ACLs are concerning because some EU PII buckets were public-once. It was an accidental policy rip when we rolled a terraform change.
[00:40] Daniel Wu: We rotated creds right after the test but we need a better guardrail. That's on me to add a policy into the pipeline.
[00:50] Alex Chen: Right, so remediation categories: immediate hotfixes (rotate, lock down ACLs), then medium term (RBAC review, SSO enforcement), and longer (KMS/HSM integration). We'll go through timing.
[01:05] Marta Reyes: And we also need audit logs — retention and the ability to query quickly for incidents. Our compliance team needs 13 months retention for EU data per contract.
[01:15] Priya Nair: Understood. Redwood's audit logs can be exported to your SIEM — currently default 90 days in-hosted but you can configure long-term retention to s3 or a customer bucket. Note that dedicated/private setups let you keep logs in your VPC as well.
[01:35] Leah Kim: Are those logs tamper-evident? We need to show integrity for SOC2.
[01:40] Alex Chen: Good question. We support signed log exports and can integrate with HSM-backed signing if you go Dedicated + HSM KMS. There's a couple ways: Redwood-managed KMS or customer-managed KMS via AWS KMS/HSM — both have trade-offs.
[01:55] Daniel Wu: For us, customer-managed KMS is preferable. We need keys in our account and no key material leaving our control.
[02:05] Priya Nair: That's fine — we can do a customer KMS integration for Redwood Private, and for Dedicated we support cross-account KMS grants. We'll put the exact required IAM actions in the playbook.

[02:20] (short pause)

[02:30] Alex Chen: Back to vuln mgmt — patch cadence. What's your current patching SLA for a high-sev?
[02:36] Daniel Wu: Right now, high-sev CNB/infra is 48 hours, app-level is more like 5 days. There's a backlog and some people are slow to triage.
[02:44] Leah Kim: We want to tighten app-level to 72 hours for anything scoring above 7.0. Also need a better triage process and runbook.
[02:52] Priya Nair: Our recommendation is: immediate mitigation for exploitable vuln, then a fix in 48-72 hours depending on impact; maintain a 2-week sprint for medium-low. We'll include a triage rubric in the remediation playbook (exploitability, data exposure, lateral movement paths).
[03:10] Marta Reyes: And add dependency scanning into CI — we had a transitive dependency that triggered one finding.
[03:16] Daniel Wu: We're on an older scanner right now, so we'll upgrade and add the baseline.

[03:25] Alex Chen: The pen-test report also called out session fixation on a legacy auth flow. That ties into RBAC/SSO discussion — are you migrating to SAML/Okta?
[03:33] Leah Kim: We're about 80% there; Okta SSO is on for 2 apps, but some internal admin consoles still use legacy tokens.
[03:40] Priya Nair: We recommend removing token-based admin flows or gating them behind step-up auth and RBAC checks. For Redwood integrations, we often map Okta groups to roles and restrict high-privilege calls via allow-lists.
[03:55] Marta Reyes: Also for audit, we need the ability to show who triggered an operation — not just API key id but the Okta user mapping.
[04:04] Alex Chen: Absolutely — that's part of the RBAC mapping we can help automate. We'll include a sample mapping file.

[04:15] (background noise, someone shuffling papers)

[04:25] Daniel Wu: About data residency — a few customers are EU-only and will not allow data to cross region. How does Redwood handle model routing?
[04:33] Priya Nair: We can pin routes by region and region-aware routing policies. For Private deployments we can keep everything in your EU tenant. For Hosted, we have an EU region offering but need contractual clauses for data residency.
[04:45] Leah Kim: Great. Is there any caching I should be worried about? The KV cache might accidentally persist user inputs.
[04:53] Priya Nair: We do prefix/KV caching for performance; you can disable caching per-route or set TTLs. For regulated workloads, customers typically disable persistent caching or set strict TTLs and never cache PII. We'll document safe defaults.

[05:10] Alex Chen: Now KMS specifics — the pen-test called out that some service account keys were long-lived and not rotated. If you move encryption keys into KMS with key rotation and HSM protection, that closes a big class of issues.
[05:22] Marta Reyes: We're also concerned about access controls to the KMS keys themselves. We need least-priv access, separations of duties, and audit trails.
[05:30] Priya Nair: For customer-managed KMS we recommend a KMS policy that only allows cloud functions from your staging account and requires MFA for key administration. We'll provide sample IAM statements. Also HSM-backed keys for high assurance.
[05:45] Leah Kim: Any latency impact from envelope encryption or HSM signing we should expect?
[05:50] Priya Nair: Minimal. Envelope encryption is the common pattern — only the small keystore calls hit KMS; data encryption/decryption stays local. We measured a median add of ~10-20ms for first decrypt in our Dedicated benchmark, but subsequent ops are cached. We'll include numbers in the playbook.

[06:12] (Alex reviewing notes)

[06:20] Alex Chen: Let's talk timeline. Our suggested pilot: connect your staging to Redwood Private with customer-managed KMS for one model route, run the KMS flows, and verify logs/export and patching response. Pilot duration 2 weeks. Thoughts?
[06:34] Daniel Wu: Sounds OK, need to confirm infra allocation. If we can get staging up by next week, we can start 7/13 as tentatively discussed.
[06:42] Marta Reyes: Make sure the pilot has a realistic traffic profile; we want to ensure the KV cache patterns and latency SLOs hold.
[06:50] Priya Nair: We'll provide a workload generator and a benchmark sheet. Also, to address audit readiness quickly, we can enable log signing during pilot.

[07:05] (brief cross-talk)

[07:15] Leah Kim: A couple nitty-gritty items from the pen test: 1) privileged session monitoring isn't centralized; 2) SCAN results not integrated into Jira; 3) devs have elevated keys in ephemeral envs.
[07:28] Priya Nair: For (1) we can forward admin session events to your central SIEM; (2) Redwood supports webhook integrations to create tickets for findings; (3) we recommend short-lived credentials with federation and no static key usage in dev.
[07:42] Daniel Wu: We'll accept the federation approach but need a migration plan because some pipelines expect static keys.
[07:48] Alex Chen: We'll include a migration checklist in the playbook with rollback steps.

[07:55] (background)

[08:05] Marta Reyes: For SOC2 readiness, would Redwood's logging and role mapping be sufficient or do we need separate attestations?
[08:12] Priya Nair: Redwood can provide SOC2 reports (if Hosted) and Attestation packages for Dedicated customers; for Private we can provide the artifacts and assist with mapping but your org will juggle responsibility for parts of the stack. We'll include an artifact map.
[08:28] Leah Kim: Ok, please include the list of evidence Redwood can provide vs what BlueHarbor is expected to produce.

[08:36] Alex Chen: We'll add that to the playbook.

[08:42] Marta Reyes: One more ask: the pen test flagged a queue processing service that deserialized untrusted payloads — how quickly can we get a hotfix without breaking producers?
[08:52] Priya Nair: Short term we can add validation layer and WAF rule; medium term rewrite to safe deserializers. We'll give a recommended patch and an integration test plan.

[09:05] (longer pause while team reviews document notes)

[09:20] Alex Chen: Ok let's summarize action items and owners — Leah uploads asset inventory, Priya drafts playbook with specific remediation steps and IAM snippets, Alex shares pricing and pilot scope, Daniel provisions staging. We agreed tentative dates.
[09:38] Marta Reyes: Agreed. Also please mark items that are compliance blockers vs risk mitigations so we can prioritize audits.
[09:46] Priya Nair: We'll flag the compliance-blocking items in the playbook (PII exposure, public buckets, key management issues).

[09:55] Daniel Wu: Quick Q on cost: is there an incremental cost to enabling HSM-backed keys in Dedicated?
[10:02] Alex Chen: Yes there is a premium for HSM-managed keys; we'll include a cost sheet. For the pilot we can enable an HSM-similar key or a customer-managed KMS without full HSM to validate functionality then upgrade.

[10:18] Marta Reyes: Great. I think we're aligned.
[10:22] Alex Chen: Thanks everyone. We'll share the playbook and ticket list by Monday 7/6.
[10:28] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings corrected where obvious; there may still be small errors (product name typos, timestamps approximate).
